description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian classic, famous for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce and tender pieces of chicken. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it a comforting and satisfying meal. It is a perfect choice for a hearty lunch or a special dinner, often served with naan or rice.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/4 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook in batches until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside. It does not need to be fully cooked through at this stage, as it will simmer in the sauce.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and saute until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1/2 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato and Cashew Mixture
instructions.text: Stir in the pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), cumin powder, coriander powder, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder. Add a pinch of salt and sugar. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are cooked down and the oil starts to separate.

instructions.title: Blend and Combine
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until very smooth. If too thick, add a splash of water. Pour the smooth sauce back into the pan. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce and stir to combine. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking.

instructions.title: Finish and Garnish
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream, the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, and the crushed Kasuri Methi. Cook for 2-3 minutes more, without boiling, until the sauce is heated through and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro before serving.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the marinated chicken slightly in a tandoor or under a broiler before adding to the sauce.
Soaking cashews is crucial for achieving a super smooth and creamy sauce texture. You can also use almond flour as a substitute for a similar richness.
Always add cream and butter at the very end and avoid boiling the sauce vigorously afterward to prevent the cream from splitting and maintain its rich texture.
article:
Mastering the Art of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian curry, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture and tantalizingly complex flavors, has transcended borders to become a global culinary sensation. If you're looking for an Indian lunch recipe that promises both comfort and an explosion of taste, look no further. We'll guide you through creating an authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani that will impress even the most discerning palates, transforming your kitchen into a hub of aromatic delight.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi in the 1950s, it was supposedly created by Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant. The dish features succulent pieces of chicken, traditionally tandoor-cooked (though pan-seared works perfectly at home), simmered in a velvety tomato-based sauce. This sauce is what truly defines Murgh Makhani: a masterful blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices, enriched generously with butter and cream. Its hallmark is its mild sweetness, subtle tang, and incredibly smooth, luxurious mouthfeel, making it a favorite for those who appreciate nuanced flavors over intense heat. It stands as a testament to the sophisticated culinary traditions of North India, offering a comforting yet elegant Indian lunch option.

## Ingredients You Need

To embark on your Butter Chicken journey, gathering the right ingredients is crucial. Quality makes a noticeable difference in the final taste of this beloved dish.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (equal parts ginger and garlic)
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp salt
*   1 tbsp lemon juice

**For the Makhani (Butter Chicken) Sauce:**
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (for creaminess)
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp cumin powder
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/4 tsp fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tsp sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Creating the perfect Butter Chicken involves a few key stages, each contributing to its legendary flavor.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for maximum flavor absorption.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken until nicely browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil. Once the butter melts, add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Flavor:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree), soaked cashews, red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes darken and the oil starts to separate, indicating the spices have cooked well.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the entire sauce mixture to a blender. Add 1/2 cup water or chicken broth. Blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra silken texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for that restaurant-style smoothness in your Butter Chicken.
6.  **Simmer and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Stir in the crushed fenugreek leaves, sugar, and salt to taste. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce.
7.  **Add Cream and Garnish:** Remove from heat. Stir in the heavy cream. Do not boil after adding cream, as it can curdle. Taste and adjust seasonings if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is now ready to serve!

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is easier with a few insider tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, creating juicy, succulent pieces that stand up to the rich sauce.
*   **Sear, Don't Boil:** When cooking the chicken, ensure you sear it quickly to develop a beautiful crust and lock in moisture. Avoid overcooking it at this stage, as it will continue to cook in the sauce.
*   **Toast Your Spices:** Cooking the spices with the tomatoes until the oil separates (bhunao) is essential. This process deepens their flavor and removes any raw taste, contributing significantly to the sauce's complexity.
*   **Smoothness is Supreme:** Blending the sauce until absolutely smooth, and then passing it through a sieve, is the secret to the signature velvety texture of Murgh Makhani. Don't skip this step if you want a truly luxurious sauce.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Fenugreek Leaves):** These dried leaves are non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils. They impart a unique, slightly bitter-sweet note that elevates the dish.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** The perfect Butter Chicken strikes a balance between sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar and salt at the end to achieve your desired equilibrium.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments.

*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan bread is the quintessential companion, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the luscious sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Aromatic basmati rice, either plain or lightly spiced (like jeera rice), provides a wonderful contrast and helps soak up the rich flavors.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber or mint raita (yogurt dip) offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad of sliced onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers dressed with lemon juice adds freshness and crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is divine, don't hesitate to experiment:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** For a vegetarian twist, swap chicken for paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly and sear before adding to the sauce.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** Use coconut cream or cashew cream instead of heavy cream, and plant-based butter for a dairy-free version. Ensure your yogurt for marination is also dairy-free.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your preference. For more heat, add green chilies along with ginger-garlic paste. For less, reduce the chili powder or omit it and rely on Kashmiri chili for color.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you have access to a grill or tandoor, grilling the marinated chicken before adding it to the sauce will infuse it with an incredible smoky depth. Alternatively, a drop of liquid smoke or a charcoal smoke treatment (dhungar) can mimic this effect.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its comforting warmth and exquisite flavors make it an ideal Indian lunch recipe for any occasion, from a quick family meal to an impressive dinner party. With this comprehensive guide, you're now equipped to create a masterpiece that will have everyone asking for seconds. Enjoy the rich, creamy, and utterly delicious journey of making your own authentic Butter Chicken!
